title: Brevo Homepage Teardown: Jan 2023 to Jun 2026
h1: How Brevo rewrote its homepage over 3 years
metaTitle: Brevo Homepage CRO Teardown — Jan 2023 to Jun 2026
description: A CRO teardown of Brevo's homepage from Jan 2023 to Jun 2026 — what changed in headline, section headings, CTAs, navigation, and what SaaS teams can study from it.
excerpt: Brevo's homepage didn't just get updated. The headline, section headings, CTAs, navigation all shifted in a consistent direction between Jan 2023 and Jun 2026. This teardown maps what changed, when, and what the patterns may suggest.
author: Wael Aouididi
authorBio: SaaS Growth Marketer and fractional growth lead. I help B2B SaaS founders diagnose landing page, CRO, positioning, and analytics leaks before scaling traffic.
featuredImageAlt: Brevo Jan 2023 homepage — 'Connections that spark growth'

messagingChanges.before: Brevo helps you grow your business. Build customer relationships across email, SMS, chat, and more. Use the tools you need, when you need them. Try it for free.

messagingChanges.note: The new description is shorter and more neutral in tone. Whether this is intentional de-emphasis or a simplification pass is not determinable from text alone.

analysisBlocks.label: Jan 2023 — original state
analysisBlocks.heading: The original: growth-outcome messaging
annotations: H1 opens with: "Connections that spark growth" — accessible benefit language aimed at a broad audience.
Visible section headings include: "Wide reachClose connection", "Everyone can grow with Brevo".
Section headings later removed include: "Wide reachClose connection" and "Everyone can grow with Brevo".

analysisBlocks.label: Jun 2026 — current state
analysisBlocks.heading: Today: updated positioning
annotations: H1 now reads: "Turn Every EmailSMSOrder Interaction into a Lifetime Customer" — updated value proposition.
New section headings include: "Join 600,000+ customers around the world who trust Brevo", "Engage your audience your way", "AI agents that work with you, and for you".
Third-party validation visible in section headings: "Awarded for excellence".
CTAs no longer present include: "Get Brevo", "Read customer stories", "See all integrations".

lessonCards.title: Your H1 signals which buyer you are targeting
lessonCards.body: The headline changed from "Connections that spark growth" to "Turn Every EmailSMSOrder Interaction into a Lifetime Custome...". The framing of your H1 is one of the clearest signals of which buyer you are targeting and what you expect them to do next.

lessonCards.title: Navigation is a positioning statement
lessonCards.body: Navigation items changed from "Products", "Features", "Email marketing" to "Platform", "Email", "SMS". The labels your navigation uses reveal what you think your visitor is trying to decide — and who that visitor is.

lessonCards.title: Section headings reveal what the team thinks buyers care about
lessonCards.body: 9 section headings were added and 2 removed between Jan 2023 and Jun 2026. New headings include "Join 600,000+ customers around the world who trust Brevo" and "Engage your audience your way". Headings that disappeared include "Wide reachClose connection" and "Everyone can grow with Brevo". The pattern of what gets added and removed is one of the clearest signals of how a team is re-prioritizing its value proposition.

lessonCards.title: Incremental changes compound into a brand shift
lessonCards.body: Across 2 snapshots spanning roughly 3 years, no single update here was a dramatic overhaul. The end state looks very different from the start because small, consistent changes in the same direction accumulate. This is worth studying if your own homepage has been drifting without a clear direction.
